message.content:
You are an ADVERSARIAL VERIFIER in a multi-agent pre-order PCB audit (Dual-Radio LoRa Sensor Node rev A; ESP32-S3, dual SX1262
915 MHz modules, W5500+PoE, GNSS, sensors; 8-layer, 160x100 mm). Read /tmp/claude-0/-root-netplan/4726c1d0-dd6d-442f-817b-15139e399d8a/scratchpad/audit-pack/README.md first (data files, rules, adjudicated items).
A finder in dimension "dfm-fab-package" claims:

{
 "id": "dfm-fab-package#9",
 "title": "Two 3V3_1 vias 0.223 mm wall-to-wall (0.523 mm centre spacing, overlapping 0.6 mm pads) — below PCBWay's 11 mil (0.28 mm) via-to-via minimum",
 "severity": "MEDIUM",
 "confidence": "high",
 "refs": [
  "C68",
  "U4"
 ],
 "nets": [
  "3V3_1"
 ],
 "location": "vias (68.75,49.857) and (69.25,49.7035), both 0.30 drill / 0.60 pad, inside the C68/U4.AVDD in-pad group",
 "evidence": "vias.tsv; centre distance sqrt(0.5^2+0.1535^2)=0.523 mm; wall gap 0.223 mm; board rule min_hole_to_hole 0.2 so DRC passes. PCBWay: 'Hole to hole spacing >= 11MIL for vias (<=0.45mm)'; advanced '<13mil special review'. Next-closest pairs are 0.34-0.35 mm.",
 "failure_scenario": "Drill wander or the second drill hitting the first barrel: a plating void in one of the U4 AVDD plane-reach vias (an endgame airwire via — the only reach for that pin), or a CAM EQ on the whole order.",
 "recommendation": "Delete one of the two (same net, same pad) or move to >= 0.63 mm centre spacing; re-run check-plugged-vias.py and update the FAB-NOTES count.",
 "needs_datasheet": ""
}

Your job is to try to REFUTE it. LENS A — RE-MEASURE. Independently re-derive the claim from the raw board data in the pack (netlist.txt, pads.tsv,
tracks.tsv, vias.tsv, zones.json, footprints.tsv, texts.json, board.json, renders, the BOM/pos in /root/hardware/boards/lora-sensor-node/fab-out and the docs). Do NOT trust the
finder's numbers, refs or coordinates — recompute them. Check the refs exist, the nets are what the finder says, the geometry/values are as claimed.
If the claim rests on a datasheet parameter, take it as stated for this lens unless the pack/docs contradict it (lens B checks datasheets).

Return: verdict = 'confirmed' (holds as stated), 'amended' (real, but severity/details/fix need correction — put the corrected statement in
amendment and the corrected severity in severity_after), 'refuted' (wrong, duplicate of an adjudicated item, or not a defect — say exactly why),
or 'unverifiable' (cannot be decided without something you could not obtain — name it). Cite files/refs/values for your evidence. Be concrete
and honest; a false refutation of a real defect costs the owner a dead board, a false confirmation costs a respin.
Do not modify any file under /root/hardware/boards/lora-sensor-node, /root/hardware, or brokkr /srv; scratch only in /tmp/claude-0/-root-netplan/4726c1d0-dd6d-442f-817b-15139e399d8a/scratchpad/audit-results/verify/ or /tmp/audit-verify/ on brokkr.

- andvari-release-sign: The andvari release ceremony split between huginn and PRESTIGE — what huginn can sign and publish itself, what genuinely requires the owner's Windows box, and the exact prompt to hand over. Use when cutting an andvari release, re-signing /downloads/manifest.json, building the MSI, or when a release is half-published.
- artistsadventure-dev: House conventions and gotchas for Artists' Adventure (AA) site work — copy style, dark-theme band rules, publish/deploy loop, owner design taste, shot-verification. Use for any artistsadventure / AA / theartistsadventure.com / silencelen.com site or editor-panel task.
- bybrynn-deploy: bybrynn.com dev/prod deploy loop on CT 121 hermod — branch tracking (b6.x → dev, main → prod), 5-min auto-pull cron, read-only deploy key, and the promotion flow. Use for any bybrynn site deploy, promotion, or deploy-debugging task.
- cloudflare-ops: Cloudflare work across all the zones — DNS records, proxying, WAF, cache and Bot Fight Mode — through the pinned cf-api.sh caller. Use for any CF DNS/zone/WAF/API change or when a site is 5xx-ing through Cloudflare. For the origin nginx side use bybrynn-deploy or artistsadventure-dev; for status-page incidents start with incident-triage.
- context-audit: Performance-audit everything auto-loaded into netplan Claude Code sessions — CLAUDE.md staleness vs the SSOT, MEMORY.md size, MCP server health/credentials, settings permissions bloat. Use when sessions feel heavy, when the user asks to audit/optimize the session context or "make sessions cleaner", or quarterly as hygiene.
- fleet-audit: Run the recurring blind, read-only, per-target security/ops audit of the heimdall fleet (the "heimdall fleet audit" ritual, 5 run so far). Use when the user asks for a fleet/security/full audit of the homelab or a machine subset. Multi-agent — expects an ultracode/workflow opt-in for full runs.
- grafana-ops: Working with the Grafana/Prometheus/Loki monitoring stack (VM 112 "mimir", .2.10:3000) — alert-rule editing traps, provisioned-rule deletion, exporter rules, token management. Use when creating/editing/debugging Grafana alerts, dashboards, or exporters. If mimir itself is slow, unreachable or looks like it needs a restart, use mimir-ops instead — restarting VM 112 is operator-only.
- headless-verify: Driving a browser headlessly on huginn to actually see a web change work — the socket-denied constraint, the pipe-CDP recipe, and the request-interception upgrade that lets a page talk to a real backend. Use when verifying any web UI, taking before/after shots, or E2E-checking a change from this host. For driving the owner's Android phone instead, see the huginn-android-app memory; for Grafana dashboards use grafana-ops.
- huginn-cli: Distribution, sync, and update workflow for the huginn-cli client (the huginn/rclaude/rcc command on phone/laptop devices) — canonical repo, huginn-sync mirror rules, device update paths, ssh -tt PTY gotcha. Use when editing, syncing, distributing, or troubleshooting the huginn CLI client or its mirrors.
- huginn-product-release: Shipping any version of the huginn product from /opt/huginn — the Android app, the Compose desktop client, the appd daemon, or the CLI/server core. Covers which script owns which component, the namespaced tags, the changelog gate, and the re-cut rules. Use when cutting or re-cutting a release, when a release is half-published, or when versions have drifted apart. For distributing the CLI to phones and laptops (huginn-sync, device updates) use huginn-cli instead.
- incident-triage: First-checks playbook for status-page incidents, monitor-down alerts, and 🔴 escalations — per-symptom diagnostic signatures learned from past incidents. Use when investigating any outage, down alert, status-page incident, or unexplained 🔴, BEFORE forming a theory or restarting anything.
- local-llm: Delegate a task to the homelab's local AI tier (huginn-llm) instead of spending Claude — when to, when not to, and how the lane behaves.
- memory-maintenance: Audit and compress huginn's file-memory (MEMORY.md index + fact files + ARCHIVE.md). Use when the user asks to clean/compress/prune memory, when MEMORY.md exceeds ~10 KB, or after a burst of sessions leaves long hooks and resolved sagas in the index.
- mempalace-ops: Operating MemPalace on muninn (LXC 118) — writing diaries through the wrapper, the daemon job queue, HNSW divergence, index rebuilds, and the read-only-MCP posture. Use when a diary or mine fails, the daemon looks wedged, vector search degrades, or someone proposes retiring the read-only flag. For curating the file-memory index instead (MEMORY.md, fact files, ARCHIVE.md) use memory-maintenance.
- mimir-ops: Operating VM 112 "mimir" (.2.10, monitoring stack + public status page origin) — the operator-only restart constraint, hung-VM signature and probes, blast radius, deploy methods, and postgres-mcp container hygiene. Use for any task touching mimir/VM112, when mimir is slow/unreachable, or when the status page is 530. For alert-rule and dashboard editing use grafana-ops; for building or deploying the status page itself use statuspage-dev.
- n8n-ops: Working on the n8n automation VM (114 "norn", Docker, VLAN 2 .2.114) — Code-node builtin restrictions, CLI workflow import/activation, webhook debugging. Use when creating/editing/debugging n8n workflows or their alerting paths. For the Grafana alert-RULE side of an alerting path use grafana-ops; for the send rules use telegram-notify.
- pbs-restore-dr: Router for backup/restore/DR situations — which runbook and script applies when a guest needs restoring, heimdall is down, PBS sync breaks, or quorum is lost. Use for any backup, restore, failover, or disaster-recovery task. Points to runbooks; does not duplicate them.
- proxmox-provisioning: Creating, cloning or converting a VM or LXC anywhere on the Proxmox fleet, and the onboarding a new guest needs before it counts as real — notes field, DNS, monitoring, backups, SSOT row. Use when standing up any guest or a lab pool, or when a guest exists but was never wired up. For reaching an existing guest use remote-ops; for restore/DR use pbs-restore-dr.
- remote-ops: How to reach every host/VM/LXC in the homelab fleet from huginn — jump paths, guest-agent vs SSH vs pct exec, known UDM inter-VLAN blocks, name mapping. Use whenever a task needs to run commands on any fleet machine, or when a connection unexpectedly fails/hangs.
- skill-forge: Turn a solved, repeatable procedure from this session into a house skill — draft it to a pending queue for owner approval, never straight into the live tree. Use when a session worked out something non-obvious that will recur, when the owner says "make this a skill", or when a trap keeps being re-derived from memory files. For AUTHORING quality use the skill-creator plugin; this skill decides whether it should exist, where it lands, and who approves it.
- statuspage-dev: Building and deploying the public status page (the status-page submodule → VM 112 mimir) — the admin-UI-config doctrine, the deploy loop with its rollback tag, and the build traps that have bitten. Use for any status-page feature, admin-panel, schema or deploy work. For mimir VM health, hangs and the restart prohibition use mimir-ops; for triaging an actual incident or a 🔴 alert use incident-triage.
- telegram-audit: Review the Telegram message stream sent to the operator over a window — delivery failures, alert storms, noise, and real action items. Use when the user asks to review/audit telegram logs, messages, alerts, or "the stream", or for the ~weekly stream audit. For SENDING rules use telegram-notify instead.
- telegram-notify: House rules for sending Telegram alerts/notifications from the homelab — send-telegram.sh usage, mandatory logging, the single-bot/single-chat policy, and when to route via n8n instead. Use when escalating, alerting, or building anything that messages the operator. For REVIEWING what was already sent (stream audits, alert noise) use telegram-audit instead.
- udm-api-ops: Talking to the UDM (UniFi OS gateway) over its API — auth, the zone-based firewall endpoints, DHCP reservations, and which legacy endpoints lie to you. Use for any UniFi firewall, DHCP, VLAN, WAN or syslog/SIEM task. For reaching hosts behind the UDM use remote-ops; for the Loki side of UDM syslog use grafana-ops.
- skill-creator:skill-creator: Create new skills, modify and improve existing skills, and measure skill performance. Use when users want to create a skill from scratch, edit, or optimize an existing skill, run evals to test a skill, benchmark skill performance with variance analysis, or optimize a skill's description for better triggering accuracy.
- design: Create a design canvas - a multi-artboard visual design published as an Artifact that runs Claude Design's canvas editor (an early preview of Claude Design inside Claude Code). You DRAFT the design as .dc.html artboards laid out on one pan/zoom canvas; where saving is enabled for the user's account they refine every element visually (click-to-select, a properties panel, inline text editing, undo/redo) and Save publishes a new version for everyone, otherwise they get a view-and-export (PNG/PDF) preview of your draft. Good for UI mockups and screen flows, landing pages, marketing and social graphics, and print pieces - posters, flyers, brochures as single-page artboards; memos and reports as one flowing artboard. Use when someone wants a design, mockup, wireframe, UI or screen design, landing page, poster, flyer, brochure, banner, card, one-pager, or any visual layout they would rather tweak by hand than in code. Only for CREATING or re-seeding a canvas; an existing one is edited in its published Artifact.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts. - Load before writing any artifact, including a skill-instructed Markdown one - Markdown is never a shortcut past the design pass.
- artifact-diagramming: Diagramming know-how for Artifacts - when a picture earns its place, how to draw one that shows the real mechanism, and the inline-SVG mechanics that keep it legible in both themes.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever the user asks for an artifact needing any such runtime behavior.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. Also use when the user wants a one-time scheduled run ("run this once at 3pm", "remind me to check X tomorrow").
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- workflow-authoring: Reference for writing a Workflow tool script (script API and gotchas, resume, quality patterns, worked examples). Load before authoring a script for a workflow the user already opted into; it does not itself authorize running one.
- claude-in-chrome: Automates your Chrome browser to interact with web pages - clicking elements, filling forms, capturing screenshots, reading console logs, and navigating sites. Opens pages in new tabs within your existing Chrome session. Requires site-level permissions before executing (configured in the extension). - When the user wants to interact with web pages, automate browser tasks, capture screenshots, read console logs, or perform any browser-based actions. Always invoke BEFORE attempting to use any mcp__claude-in-chrome__* tools.
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch
